proposed.text: A building owner proposes to change a building's use to a classification that is LESS hazardous than its current use. Under Sec. 702, what level of authority may approve this change?

options.text: The DPWH Regional Director must approve all changes of occupancy regardless of hazard direction
The Building Official alone may approve a change to a less hazardous use classification
The local Zoning Administrator has exclusive authority over all occupancy reclassifications
No approval is needed for changes to less hazardous uses; only the owner's written declaration is required

proposed.rationale: Sec. 702 provides that when the proposed change is to a use of LESSER hazard, the Building Official — as the sole authority at the local level — may approve the change. The BO evaluates whether the building meets the Code requirements for the new, less hazardous use and exercises discretion to approve. Changes to MORE hazardous uses require full Code compliance and a more rigorous review process.
proposed.explanation: The BO is the SOLE authority for occupancy change approvals. For less hazardous changes, the BO may approve using discretion. For more hazardous changes, full Code compliance is mandatory before the BO can approve. The DPWH is not the approving authority for individual building occupancy changes.
